plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Do Docta-cleaned labels show higher credibility (improved predictive performance) than raw labels, validated by ChatGPT and in-house human annotators on disagreements?"

1. OVERVIEW & HYPOTHESIS
H1 (two-sided to falsification, tested conjunctively): On a fixed-model protocol with identical splits/hyperparameters, models trained on Docta-cleaned labels (arm C) achieve higher held-out predictive performance than models trained on raw labels (arm R), AND, separately and independently, on the raw↔cleaned disagreement subset, both ChatGPT and in-house human annotators each favor the cleaned label more often than the raw label. H1 is therefore a conjunctive claim with a single pre-specified verdict (see §3).

Arms: R (train on raw labels), C (train on Docta-cleaned labels), optional reference arm A (train on dual-validator-adjudicated labels), all holding the SAME base model, hyperparameters, train/val/test partitions, seeds, and test class priors. The optional arm A is descriptive only (never the object of the headline claim), included to check whether adjudicated labels beat both R and C.

2. DATASET & PREPROCESSING (defaults to be confirmed per topic)
- N total instances of a supervised task (assumption: classification; regression variant noted in §7). Split 70/10/20 train/val/test (default), identical partition object used for both arms to make every run paired. Test priors matched.
- D = {instances where raw label ≠ cleaned label}. If Docta drops instances ("cleaning" = relabel+drop), handle explicitly: model trained on Docta's emitted instance set; a parallel R′ model trained on raw labels restricted to Docta's surviving instance IDs is the comparability control against a naive R-on-all-instances baseline (§6). Both interpretations reported.
- If |D| > n_D, draw a stratified random sample (default n_D = 300, ≤400 budget cap) for validator adjudication; else use all of D.

3. COMMIT 1 — PRIMARY ENDPOINT & PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE
Decision: predictive performance is the PRIMARY quantitative endpoint; validator agreement is a REQUIRED co-primary corroboration. The headline claim "cleaned labels are more credible" is supported only if the performance leg AND each validator leg independently pass. The two validators are NEVER merged into a single "consensus truth"; they are three separate legs (performance, human, ChatGPT), with validator-vs-validator agreement reported only as a consistency diagnostic.

Primary performance endpoint (single metric, pre-specified): held-out macro-F1 on the identical test set, Δ_i = macroF1(C)_i − macroF1(R)_i per run.

Runs: S=5 seeds × K=5 independent splits = 25 paired runs (each split shared by R and C; seeds vary init/data-order only).

Pre-registered decision rule (thresholds are defaults, locked before results are seen; they are to be re-confirmed with the concrete dataset at the calibration step, but the logic and legs are fixed):
- PERFORMANCE LEG (P): pass iff (i) mean Δ ≥ δ_min = +1.0 pp macro-F1; (ii) one-sided bootstrap 95% CI lower bound on mean Δ > 0; (iii) paired Wilcoxon signed-rank over the 25 runs, two-sided p < 0.05.
- HUMAN LEG (H): on the sampled D, human-majority adjudication (3 annotators, expert tie-break) sides with the cleaned label on ≥ 60% of items, with one-sided 95% Wilson lower bound > 55%, and cleaned-favoring > raw-favoring in a paired binomial test (p < 0.05) counting "neither" conservatively as non-clean-favoring.
- CHATGPT LEG (G): same thresholds as H, computed from ChatGPT's independent judgments (temperature 0, fixed prompt), never informed of H's outcome.
- VERDICT:
  · H1 SUPPORTED iff P ∧ H ∧ G all pass.
  · P passes but H and/or G fail → "PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (performance evidence only, validator corroboration absent)" — explicitly NOT counted as success.
  · P fails (regardless of H/G) → "NOT SUPPORTED" (performance is primary; validator legs alone are insufficient).
  · H and G strongly contradict (e.g., cohen's kappa < 0.2 on D) → force a MIXED-EVIDENCE verdict even if P∧H∧G numerically pass (pre-registered failure of the dual-validator design premise).
Every verdict is reported with the three legs' statistics reported separately.

4. COMMIT 2 — BOTH GROUND-TRUTH SCENARIOS
Scenario (i) GOLD/HELD-OUT TEST SET EXISTS:
- Evaluation reference = the independent gold test set (never used for training or cleaning).
- Protocol: train R and C with identical pipeline; evaluate both on the identical gold test set. Δ(macro-F1) is measured against gold → unbiased generalization comparison.
- Label-level credibility check: accuracy of raw vs cleaned labels directly against gold labels on the test set (does cleaning move labels toward gold?). If gold overlaps D, raw-vs-clean on gold is the strongest "who is right" evidence.
- Interpretation: strongest form of the claim; predictive performance on gold = unbiased estimate; Δ is the headline effect; validator legs still run on D (train-side) as the question requires, but gold is the authoritative arbiter where available.
Scenario (ii) NO GOLD TEST SET EXISTS:
- No independent reference. Held-out test portion is still (raw- and cleaned-) labeled, but evaluating both arms on raw labels would bias toward R, and on cleaned labels would be circular toward C. Therefore:
- The held-out test split's reference is CONSTRUCTED by the dual-validator protocol: human-majority adjudication (3 humans, expert tie-break) on the full test split gives the pseudo-gold reference; ChatGPT adjudication over the same split is computed as a parallel reference for sensitivity.
- Metrics: same primary macro-F1 of R vs C evaluated against the human-adjudicated test reference; accuracy/AUC as secondary; label-level credibility = proximity: cleaned-vs-reference accuracy vs raw-vs-reference accuracy on held-out.
- Interpretation (must be explicitly weaker): claims are conditional on the adjudicated reference — evidence that C generalizes at least as well to the validated portion and that cleaned labels sit closer to validator-established truth. Every report under (ii) carries the caveat "no gold standard; reference is constructed". The design reports results under BOTH references (human-based and ChatGPT-based) as a sensitivity table, never pooled into one number. If scenario (i) gold labels are obtainable even partially, the subset with gold is analyzed under (i) rules.

5. DUAL-VALIDATOR DISAGREEMENT-RESOLUTION PROTOCOL (numbers included)
- D sample: n_D = 300 stratified by class (cap 400; all D if smaller).
- In-house humans: m = 3 independent annotators per item; each sees item + "Label A"/"Label B" (source-blind, order randomized/counterbalanced across items and annotators); a third distinct label may be entered. Adjudicated label = majority of 3; if no majority, senior/expert annotator (pre-defined person or a documented rule of selecting the label matching the task gold-standard description) tie-breaks.
- ChatGPT: fixed model version, temperature 0, one seeded run, fixed prompt template mirroring the human task exactly (same source-blind A/B framing); output parsed programmatically; no human feedback loop. ChatGPT never sees human answers.
- Coding for analysis: per item, human outcome ∈ {favor-cleaned, favor-raw, neither}; ChatGPT outcome ∈ {favor-cleaned, favor-raw, neither}; "neither" counted conservatively against cleaned (§3). Consistency diagnostics: cohen's kappa (human vs ChatGPT on D), and % of D where both favor cleaned.
- Budget note: Scenario (i) annotates n_D≈300; Scenario (ii) additionally adjudicates the full held-out test split (cap e.g. 400–1000 items) to construct the reference.

6. CONTROLS
- Baseline: arm R (raw labels) is the explicit baseline for Δ; additionally a random-label and majority-class classifier gives floor performance for context.
- Fixed protocol: identical base model, hyperparameters, tokenizer/features, optimizer, splits, seeds, evaluation script across arms.
- Comparability control for instance-mismatch (§2): R′ trained on raw labels restricted to Docta surviving IDs, to separate "cleaning benefit" from "dropping noisy instances benefit"; both R′ and R reported against C (and A).
- Blinding: ChatGPT and humans never see which label is raw vs cleaned ("A/B" presentation).
- Order randomization & counterbalancing: item order and A/B position randomized and counterbalanced across annotators and ChatGPT runs.
- Annotation quality gates: 5% gold/attention items injected (≥95% pass to retain annotator); double-annotated quality subset → Fleiss' kappa ≥ 0.60 on D-adjudications, else annotator re-training/requalification before analysis.
- Pre-registration: hypotheses, metrics, thresholds (§3), and analysis code locked before results; multiple-comparison control via single primary metric (macro-F1 primary; accuracy and AUC secondary/descriptive only).

7. ANALYSIS / STATISTICAL PLAN
- Primary inference: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (two-sided, p<0.05) on the 25 run-level Δ(macro-F1) values; bootstrap 95% CIs (stratified by run) on mean Δ; McNemar test on paired correct/incorrect predictions of the canonical seed-0 run on the fixed test set (pre-specified as a secondary paired test; the Wilcoxon is the primary because it pools seed/split variation).
- Secondary performance metrics: test accuracy and AUC reported with CIs, no formal claim (multiplicity control).
- Label-set statistics: % raw↔cleaned disagreement, cohen's kappa (raw vs cleaned), per-class disagreement profile, disagreement vs class/feature correlation.
- Validator analysis: per-validator cleaned-favoring proportions with Wilson CIs; paired binomial (cleaned>raw); human-vs-ChatGPT agreement; contingency table clean/raw/neither × human/chatgpt.
- Scenario split: all §3/§7 statistics computed under both scenarios as applicable; scenario (ii) computed against both references (human-based and ChatGPT-based) in a sensitivity table.
- Regression variant (if task is regression): main metric = RMSE/MAE on held-out; Δ(RMSE) with paired t/Wilcoxon over runs; no McNemar; label-credibility = absolute deviation of raw vs cleaned labels from reference.
- Missing data / dropped instances handled per §2 with the R′ control; sensitivity: repeat Δ with cleaned-set-only train instances for both arms.

8. FEASIBILITY
- This is a DESIGN-ONLY task: no execution, repository, installed ML libraries, network, GPU, or dataset is required to produce this design; the workspace contains only task.json and the plan is fully specified above.
- Concrete execution (Docta run, ChatGPT API calls, annotator platform, model training) would be carried out later in an environment with network + compute + the real dataset; the design is written to be runnable there (fixed seeds, pre-registered thresholds, exact metric/rule definitions).
- NO experiment has been run, and no result is claimed; every number above is a pre-registered threshold, not an outcome.

9. ASSUMPTIONS (explicitly NOT facts; none are confirmed by any workspace source)
- A1 Docta = a label-cleaning method producing a cleaned label set from a raw-labeled dataset; whether it relabels only vs also flags/drops instances is assumed and parametrized (§2 handles both).
- A2 A supervised dataset/task of size N exists with raw labels; exact task, size, class balance unknown.
- A3 "Credibility" = improvement in held-out predictive performance under a fixed protocol + independent validator agreement (this operationalization is the design's commitment, marked as a definitional assumption).
- A4 When raw/cleaned disagree, reference truth = human adjudication; ChatGPT is a separate corroborator, never merged (committed by the researcher).
- A5 Annotator pool: ≥3 in-house annotators with qualification criteria (≥95% gold, kappa ≥ 0.6); exact headcount/selection unknown.
- A6 Base model: a fixed off-the-shelf model appropriate to the task (the concrete choice to be set once the task is known).
- A7 ChatGPT: API with fixed model version, temperature 0, fixed prompt; availability/budget unknown (network disabled here).
- A8 Raw and cleaned label sets cover the same instance universe; instance-subset mismatch (if Docta drops) is parametrized rather than assumed away.
- A9 Labels in raw data contain enough noise to produce a meaningful D (≥ some dozens of disagreements) for validator legs.

10. CLARIFICATIONS FOR THE RESEARCHER (topic-driven; design uses the defaults above until answered)
- Concrete dataset/task (classification vs regression) and N; whether any gold/held-out labels exist (chooses §4 scenario (i) vs (ii), possibly both).
- Docta's exact cleaning behavior (relabel-only vs drop/flag) and whether it needs a validation set or outputs confidence/quality scores.
- ChatGPT model version/API availability & query budget; annotator pool size/expertise and annotation budget.
- Calibration of δ_min and validator thresholds to the task (the logic/legs stay fixed; only numeric margins are re-affirmed once task difficulty is known).

context.question: Do the labels cleaned by Docta demonstrate higher credibility—reflected in improved predictive performance—compared to raw labels, as validated by both ChatGPT and in-house human annotators when disagreements occur between the two sets?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
